docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • This datasheet is meant to document the process of the temperature sensing portion and displaying of information of Project B.A.M.F's plant moniter.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
• The temperature sensor is a part of this project to detect how hot or cold the area around the plant moniter is. This information will be used for display and will also be sent to a seperate board that will be able to activate or deactivate a motor with a fan attached. This allows the user to moniter the temperature and other information such as light level and moisture that is sent from other boards.
  • This sensor works by taking the temperature with two internal crystal oscillators, one with a low temperature coeffecient and one with a high temperature coeffecient. The difference is then taken and converted from analog to digital internally and the temperature is given through the one information pin.
  • For more information about the entire project, please click here.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This block diagram illustrates the temperature and display portion of the plant monitoring system, including its power distribution, sensors, microcontroller, actuators, and team connections. A 9V, 1.3A wall adapter supplies power to an L7805 voltage regulator, which provides a regulated 5V supply to the system. The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano serves as the central controller, receiving digital temperature measurements from the DS18B20 and analog signals from additional sensors through its ADC inputs. The controller processes the collected data and communicates with the OLED display through UART while also controlling output devices such as the status LED. Shared digital and analog connectors allow the different team-developed subsystems to interface with the main controller.

I connect to all three of the boards, recieving information from one and two and sending information to three.

docs.title: Temperature Sensor
docs.text:
1 DS18B20

  • $6.93/each

  • DS18B20

Pros Cons 1. Digital output (easy MCU connection). 1. Requires 1-Wire communication. 2. ±0.5°C accuracy. 2. Slower temperature conversion. 3. Waterproof probe options available. 3. Requires pull-up resistor.

2 ZTP-148SRC1

  • $2.06/each

  • ZTP-148SRC1

Pros Cons 1. Non-contact temperature measurement. 1. Requires additional signal processing. 2. Fast response time. 2. More difficult to calibrate. 3. Includes ambient temperature compensation. 3. Measures surface temperature, not air temperature.

3 LMT86LPM

  • $0.71/each

  • LMT86LPM

Pros Cons 1. High accuracy (±0.4°C typical). 1. Requires an analog MCU input. 2. Very low power consumption. 2. Requires temperature conversion calculations. 3. Simple analog output. 3. Sensitive to electrical noise.

Choice: DS18B20

docs.text:
1 LS013B7DH03

  • $12.39/each

  • LS013B7DH03

Pros Cons 1. Extremely low power consumption. 1. Monochrome display. 2. 128 × 128 resolution. 2. Requires specialized FPC connection. 3. Good outdoor visibility. 3. Limited visibility in darkness without backlighting.

2 NHD-C12832A1Z-FSW-FBW-3V3

  • $10.95/each

  • NHD-C12832A1Z-FSW-FBW-3V3

Pros Cons 1. Low power consumption. 1. Limited 128 × 32 resolution. 2. SPI communication. 2. Small viewing area. 3. Transflective screen for visibility in different lighting. 3. Requires external backlight power.

3 MDOB128064V2V-WI

  • $12.30/each

  • MDOB128064V2V-WI

Pros Cons 1. High contrast OLED display. 1. Higher power consumption than memory LCD. 2. 128 × 64 resolution. 2. Potential OLED burn-in. 3. Simple I2C communication. 3. More expensive than basic LCD displays.

Choice: MDOB128064V2V-WI

docs.title: Power Regulation
docs.text:
1 L7805ABV-DG

  • $1.53/each

  • L7805ABV-DG

Pros Cons 1. Fixed 5V output. 1. Generates excess heat. 2. Up to 1.5A output current. 2. Lower power efficiency. 3. Built-in thermal protection. 3. Requires heat management at higher loads.

2 NJM7805FA

  • $1.85/each

  • NJM7805FA

Pros Cons 1. Stable 5V output. 1. Generates excess heat. 2. Up to 1.5A output current. 2. Lower power efficiency. 3. Built-in short-circuit protection. 3. Requires higher input voltage than output.

3 MIC5156-3.3YN

  • $3.84/each

  • MIC5156-3.3YN

Pros Cons 1. Provides 3.3V regulation. 1. Requires an external MOSFET. 2. Low standby current. 2. More complicated circuit design. 3. Adjustable output and enable control options. 3. Requires additional external components.

Choice:L7805ABV-DG

docs.text:
This Bill of Materials documents Team B.A.M.F.'s temperature sensor module and display, with all the necessary parts (with suppliers and datasheets) per prototype unit. This serves as documentation to the necessary parts that make up the subsystem, so it can be referred to and replicated.

Some important notes: The unit quantity is how many of the component in the individual module, the unit cost is how much each individual component costs, and the total prototype cost is how much a it would cost to complete a prototype with the parts. # Ordered is extra parts for breadbaording and replacements if need be, not how many are necessary.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The purpose of the power budget was to figure out how much power each component in our plant sensor needs and make sure our power supply can handle it. I looked up the voltage and current requirements for each component, including the temperature sensor, display, voltage regulator, and microcontroller. I also compared different components to see which ones would use less power.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text: From the prepare Power Budget, the L7805ABV-DG voltage regulator is rated for up to 1.5 A, leaving approximately 845.625 mA of available current capacity on the rail. The selected 24V wall supply can provide up to 2.5 A, while the regulator is listed as drawing 1.5 A, leaving 1 A of remaining current capacity at the source. Overall, the listed current ratings suggest that the system has sufficient current capacity to operate, even with the safety margin.
